newsitem.title: FRANCE: Iraq's Aziz presses for more French UN monitors.
newsitem.headline: Iraq's Aziz presses for more French UN monitors.

text.p: Iraqi Deputy Prime Minister Tareq Aziz pressed France on Wednesday to name more officials to the U.N. Special Commission on Iraq, saying this would help reveal the extent of Baghdad's efforts to comply with U.N. resolutions.
French parliamentarians who met Aziz said he had made the demand to both Prime Minister Alain Juppe and to Foreign Minister Herve de Charette at meetings earlier this week.

De Charette urged Aziz on Tuesday to cooperate fully with the special commission and with the International Atomic Energy Authority on the removal of its weapons of mass destruction and in accounting for Kuwaiti and Saudi citizens missing since the 1991 Gulf War.

"We are working with the special commission and we will continue to work with it. We have demanded that France increase its participation so that people can know the truth," Aziz told reporters after meeting a parliamentarian's Franco-Iraqi friendship group.
"I have reaffirmed that we are hiding no weapons and the truth will come out soon. The participation of more French observers is important because they are objective," he said.

Aziz added that since an international economic embargo was imposed on Iraq in 1990, several countries had jumped in with contracts worth millions of dollars to supply oil buyers left dry by the ban on Iraqi oil exports.
"France is not a partner in this game," Aziz said.

Former Socialist Defence Minister Jean-Pierre Chevenement, a member of the parliamentary association, accused Washington of treating Iraq "not like a country with a population but like a petrol reserve...The Iraqi people are being treated like Apache Indians at the end of the 19th century".

While France favours bringing Iraq back into the international community as soon as possible, Washington and London appear reluctant to accept any major easing of the embargo as long as President Saddam Hussein remains in power.
